hook: Telangana's off-budget debt hits *₹1.21 lakh crore*, World Bank flags gaps
hook_b: Telangana's off-budget debt hits *₹1.21 lakh crore*, World Bank flags gaps
tldr: A World Bank study for the 16th Finance Commission flags inconsistencies in Telangana's off-budget borrowing disclosures.

beats.what: Telangana's outstanding off-budget liabilities were ₹1,20,944 crore at the end of 2023-24.
beats.why: Such loans are raised via state-owned entities and SPVs, so they sit outside the budget's headline debt.
beats.care: Debt repayments shape how much the state can spend on schemes, jobs and infrastructure.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: TOI: The report recommends entity-wise yearly disclosure, ideally in state budgets.

cards.q: Should states publish all off-budget loans in the budget?

qs: How much of the state's yearly revenue goes into servicing these loans?

facts.t: Kerala's off-budget liabilities were *3% of GSDP*; Karnataka's *1%*.
Telangana raised *₹2,303 crore* fresh off-budget loans in 2023-24.

learn.t: Off-budget borrowing = loans taken by state companies or SPVs, repaid with govt money, but not shown as state debt.

watch: Whether the 16th Finance Commission adopts the disclosure recommendation.

twist: Six state entities showed nil liabilities in 2022 despite ₹35,667 crore in govt guarantees.
